positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Backend engineer on the Java calculation engine behind Adaptive Planning: multi-currency consolidation, intercompany elimination, and archived versions for enterprise FP&A customers. Contracted to the same team Dec 2023 – Jun 2025 (see Magnit Global entry).

- Multi-currency consolidation (Cumulative Translation Adjustment): took over a 40%-complete rewrite, redesigned it, and finished it solo. Replaced per-cell scalar conversion with a single-pass grid that computes assigned-rate and period-end conversions side by side and takes their delta. Routed the legacy path through the new engine behind feature flags, with parity tests proving identical output before cutover. Shipping in the upcoming release.

- Intercompany elimination: designed and implemented solo, from design doc to code, a replacement for the recursive "pull" elimination engine. Trading partners are resolved once at build time into a pre-indexed pipeline, and the engine stores source coordinates rather than computed values, so intercompany amounts cancel in a vectorized pass with incremental updates and no circular-reference tracking.

- Reliability: fixed high-severity customer escalations on release branches, including numerical-correctness and metadata-caching defects that were blocking archives.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Contract software engineer on Workday's Adaptive Planning Computing Engine team, the Java calculation engine behind the product; converted to full-time at Workday in June 2025.

Archived Versions (freezing a planning version so it stays byte-stable and loads fast)
- Owned the "view error location" capability: new API endpoint, location recording in the archive path, and protobuf responses so customers can jump directly to any error in a frozen version.
- Built the tool that diffs live vs. archived model state using vectorized comparison; it caught release-blocking defects before customers hit them and eliminated false positives in data-integrity checks.
- Wrote the unit-test framework for the feature and 600+ tests, taking the subsystem to 100% coverage.

Cube columnar view, team of 3 (shows a cube sheet as one flat, sortable list of rows for bulk data entry)
- Owned the hardest part, the multi-key sort. Users sort by many keys at once; chosen keys sort by display name and every remaining key falls back to tree order, so every request returns the same total ordering. Keys are hierarchy objects rather than strings, so they are resolved once per distinct entity into fixed integer pairs and shared across rows with the same account, level, and dimension combination. The comparator works on those pairs directly instead of repeating lookups, type branching, and boxing on every one of the O(n log n) comparisons.
- Resolved linked accounts into flat rows through a multi-threaded evaluator with weighted-average rollups; enforced row-level access control with result truncation inside the evaluator.

projects.title: Belli Hunter | Autonomous AI-Assisted Trading Platform
projects.description:
Python 3.11, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, Supabase, Alpaca API, Modal, Claude API

- Serverless FastAPI service that takes TradingView webhooks through risk, research, sizing, and execution stages. A Claude agent using forced tool-use returns a structured verdict with a recorded rationale; any ambiguous or contradictory output fails closed, so no trade executes without a clean verdict.

- Position sizing, slippage tolerance, and agent strictness adapt to a market-cap and volatility tier assigned per signal.

- Safety controls: daily-loss circuit breaker, stale-signal rejection, idempotent execution, and a two-key environment interlock that blocks live trading unless both keys are set. Every signal and fill is journaled append-only and reconciled asynchronously.

- Built and tested against a paper account. Designed by me; implemented with Claude Code.

projects.title: Funnel | nightly candidate-selection and strategy-mapping pipeline
projects.description:
Python 3.11, DuckDB, Parquet, Pydantic, PyYAML, pytest, EODHD and Alpaca APIs, Claude Code

- Runs nightly on cron over the full US equity list: symbol census, bulk end-of-day ingest, universe filters, feature computation, market-regime classification, fuzzy matching of each symbol to one of four versioned strategy archetypes, within-archetype grading, and cross-sectional A/B/C tiering into a daily report with concrete trade cards.

- Designed as a selection machine, not a permission machine: continuous scores replace binary vetoes (hard vetoes capped at three), tiers are assigned by percentile so the report cannot degenerate to all-C, and the report is never empty. The nightly run makes no LLM calls, so identical inputs produce byte-identical output, verified by golden-file tests.

- Data layer audits itself: a provider adapter boundary with Pydantic-validated responses, a trailing-window revision audit that records silent provider restatements as events instead of overwriting them, a second-provider watchdog cross-check, a shadow log tracking forward return and excursion for every emitted candidate whether traded or not, and grade-distribution alarms.

- Replaced an earlier gate-based swing digest after its audits showed the code matched the spec while output stayed degenerate; that failure analysis is the design basis for the Funnel.

- Specified and designed by me; implemented with Claude Code against the spec, with every module reviewed and tested before merge.
